subject: Howison commemorative publication context
primary_or_contemporary_source: University of California Publications in Philosophy vol.1 catalogue/series notice
documented_finding: Volume I was prepared in commemoration of George Holmes Howison's seventieth birthday and lists Lovejoy's The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza at pp.141-174 with Lovejoy identified as Professor of Philosophy at Washington University.
evidence_limit: Does not establish Lovejoy attended any celebration or participated in the editorial committee.

subject: Opening historiographic problem
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.141
documented_finding: Lovejoy opens by treating the classification of Spinoza's system and its relation to historic doctrinal types as an unresolved problem and contrasts radically divergent interpretations.
evidence_limit: Does not by itself establish the later genealogical solution.

subject: Explicit methodological programme
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.145
documented_finding: Lovejoy says he will exhibit Spinoza's dialectical procedure through examination of its historical sources and affinities and comparison with Bruno.
evidence_limit: Historical affinity must not automatically be redescribed as direct borrowing.

subject: Metaphysical otherworldliness correct locator
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.151
documented_finding: Lovejoy describes Platonic transcendence as a sort of metaphysical otherworldliness and argues that internal contradiction made a movement toward inclusive monism/immanence natural or inevitable.
evidence_limit: Corrects the earlier provisional p.174 locator; phrase is on p.151.

subject: Deliberate retention of contradiction
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.153
documented_finding: Lovejoy says Neo-Platonism deliberately accepted both immanence and transcendence because both appeared equally necessary consequences of a single metaphysical principle.
evidence_limit: Does not imply Lovejoy approves the metaphysical principle.

subject: Bruno transformation of inherited system
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.160ff
documented_finding: Lovejoy distinguishes Bruno's distinctive temper emphases and corrections from continuity in the essential outlines and dialectical method of Renaissance Neo-Platonism.
evidence_limit: Continuity of method does not erase genuine doctrinal novelty.

subject: Single dialectical ground and historical source
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza pp.172-173
documented_finding: Lovejoy says Spinoza fully means both opposed conceptions because his fundamental logical principle generates both; interpretation must preserve their single dialectical ground and historic source in an ancient philosophical tradition.
evidence_limit: Does not justify reducing the article to mature unit-idea terminology.

subject: Logical and historical dual requirement
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.173
documented_finding: Lovejoy says Spinoza can be properly located in metaphysics only by understanding him both logically and historically.
evidence_limit: Logical reconstruction and historical provenance remain distinct evidentiary tasks.

subject: Philosophical moral from history
primary_or_contemporary_source: Lovejoy The Dialectic of Bruno and Spinoza p.173
documented_finding: Lovejoy draws the moral that attempts to construct a genuinely absolute Absolute that is simultaneously inclusive of all reality are hopeless.
evidence_limit: Historical genealogy and Lovejoy's own philosophical evaluation must remain distinguishable.

subject: Contemporary corroboration
primary_or_contemporary_source: H. Heath Bawden review in Journal of Philosophy Psychology and Scientific Methods 2.9
documented_finding: Bawden independently characterizes Lovejoy's essay as an analysis of contradictory elements and quotes the single dialectical ground conclusion.
evidence_limit: Now secondary corroboration rather than the controlling witness.

subject: Return to Berkeley/Howison publication network
documented_finding: Lovejoy contributed as a Washington University professor to a UC philosophy volume explicitly prepared for his former Berkeley teacher Howison.
evidence_limit: Publication participation does not prove continuing doctrinal adherence to Howison.
